LHX.sentence: L3Harris ticked up slightly, and the real question is whether its thinner-than-usual profit margins are just a temporary hangover from a recent acquisition or something more lasting — the evidence leans toward temporary, which is why it looks attractive here.

ASML.sentence: ASML is sitting right at its all-time high and barely moved today — nothing dramatic, just the quiet strength you'd expect from the only company that makes the machines needed to print the most advanced chips.

LIN.sentence: Linde is having an uneventful stretch — the industrial-gas business rolls along on long-term contracts, and it's priced right in line with its closest peers.

MSFT.sentence: Microsoft has run up sharply, far ahead of similar companies lately, on all the excitement about its cloud and AI business — nothing's wrong, it's just gotten a bit crowded and stretched.

TMO.sentence: Thermo Fisher had a decent day, and there's an encouraging sign underneath — biotech funding is thawing, which usually shows up in their lab-equipment orders a couple of quarters later.

ENB.sentence: Enbridge is quiet, moving oil and gas through its pipelines like a toll road, though the extra income it pays out isn't as generous a cushion over safe bonds as it sometimes is.

GLNCY.sentence: Glencore ticked up and is doing a bit better than pure copper miners, which suggests investors are giving it credit for its commodity-trading arm on top of the mines.

RDDT.sentence: Reddit slipped a little, but its advertising revenue is growing fast — the only real worry is whether Google keeps sending it as many visitors, since a lot of its traffic arrives that way.

KOF.sentence: Coca-Cola FEMSA drifted down slightly and looks cheap for the dominant Coke bottler in Latin America, with a steady and growing dividend.

PBR.A.sentence: Petrobras had a good day as oil prices stayed firm, which supports its famously large dividends — just keep in mind these oil earnings tend to swing with the price of crude.

AMKBY.sentence: Maersk is having an uneventful week, and its shares are priced below the value of the ships it owns — the kind of low point that tends to show up when global trade is quiet.

MA.sentence: Mastercard is flat, and oddly it's priced slightly cheaper than its twin Visa when it usually costs a bit more — meanwhile people keep tapping their cards more than ever, so the business is fine.

ISRG.sentence: The surgical robot company jumped today after being unfairly sold off — there's no sign hospitals are actually using its machines less, so the earlier weakness looks like fear rather than fact.
